verdicts.rewritten_summary: National-framework source (applies country-wide; no provincial breakdown): HRW news release, Oct 29, 2025, reports a leaked omnibus draft ("11th Judicial Package") that would amend the penal code to criminalise conduct deemed contrary to biological sex and general morality with up to three years' prison, participation in same-sex engagement or marriage ceremonies with up to four years, and would raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care including surgery from 18 to 25 with mandatory permanent infertility and repeated evaluations at government-approved hospitals; healthcare professionals performing such interventions would face fines and up to seven years in prison, and trans people receiving deemed-illegal care up to three years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association opposed the draft; HRW warns it would force treatment underground and expose people to arrest and pretrial detention.

National-framework monitoring report (applies country-wide; no provincial breakdown): Kaos GL's 2025 review finds hostility toward LGBTI+ people became explicit state policy — "Year of the Family" instructions issued to public institutions, an LGBTI+ association closed for the first time in years with criminal cases against 11 of its members, and artistic events cancelled or banned. The report documents 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings (trans people the most affected), 89 torture/ill-treatment violations (up from 51 the prior year), roughly 313 total violations overall — about 2.5 times the previous year — with 299 detention decisions, and freedom-of-expression violations rising from 216 to 540.
